pass_a_gloss: (For three, he says,) seasons of the year keep feast to me. Do you wish then, the word having already come about sufficiently for us on two, that we say what the third is, and on what it would be completed? For you inquired somewhere the occasion on each: for the one, that Christ, having endured death on behalf of the salvation of all of us, saved; and the other, that having dissolved the corruption he came back to life again, and renewed us into new life, was usefully completed. And of the first the time in the months of the year, first and at the beginnings; and of the second the neighbor at once and yoked alongside, in which it was likely that the reaping iron hurries to the ears and that the other of the seeds must be gathered together. For countless as many as of the things in fields. Come then also on the third time of the feast let us say the likely things, busying ourselves very well about how and on what it must be accomplished, and the knowledge on this let us request of the law, and let us take it from the sacred Scriptures themselves; for thus the word would go toward the truth. If I do not seem to you to say this rightly and to have considered it again? PALL.: Altogether then. CYR.: It is written then in Leviticus: 'And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: Speak to the sons of Israel saying: Of the seventh month, on one of the month, there will be for us a rest, everlasting memorial of trumpets, called holy to the Lord. Every work of service you will not do, and you will bring whole burnt offerings to the Lord.' The seventh month then seems to us to hint at the time at the consummation and at the last things. For in the seventh month all the things from fields are not to be gathered to the threshing floor from somewhere, my good man, but it would be fitting to be shut in already in the treasuries of each themselves. And the time of good crop passes by, and the beginning of winter already rises, and plants wane, and flowers wither. Come then, changing over the things from the season as on ourselves, let us say that this age already creeping toward the end, and as it were something hanging over and about to drive in, in which it is necessary that the sin-lovers be punished, each will heap up the thing from his own labors, if indeed he is sensible, and will carry it into the treasuries above. And he will remember Christ saying: 'Do not treasure for yourselves treasures on the earth, where moth and eating make disappear, and where thieves dig through and steal; but treasure rather in the heavens.' Therefore since, Christ having been raised, the words of the holy mystagogues carry us off into remembrance of the consummation, for up and down they have cried out, It is the last hour, let the things from each be gathered together, he says, into the treasuries above already, he says, for the rest. But in the new moon, he says, of the month in which you shut in the crops, there will be for you a rest, memorial of trumpets. For each treasures the good things from his own sweats, and will provide for and take care of the luxury and rest into the age, remembering that, as the divine Paul says, (continues)
pass_b_english: Cyril: …times in the year you shall keep a feast for me’ (Exodus 23:14). Now that our account of two of them has been sufficient, do you want us to say what the third is, and for what it is kept? You surely learned the reason for each. The one was fittingly kept because Christ, who endured death for the salvation of us all, has saved us; the other because he destroyed corruption, came back to life, and renewed us into a new life. And the time of the first is, among the months of the year, the first and at the beginning; the time of the second is its near neighbor, joined right to it, the time when it was natural for the reaping iron to hurry to the ears of grain and for the other kinds of seed to be gathered in, for the crops of the fields are countless. Come, then, let us say what is fitting about the season of the third feast too, inquiring closely how and on what grounds it must be accomplished. Let us ask the law for the knowledge of this, and take it from the sacred Scriptures themselves; for so our account would move toward the truth. Do I not seem to you to say and to have thought this through rightly?

Cyril: It is written, then, in Leviticus: ‘And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: In the seventh month, on the first of the month, you shall have a rest, an everlasting memorial of trumpets, a holy assembly to the Lord. You shall do no work of service, and you shall offer whole burnt offerings to the Lord’ (Leviticus 23:23–25).

The seventh month seems to us to hint at the time of the consummation and of the last things. For in the seventh month, my friend, the produce of the fields is not to be gathered from here and there to the threshing floor; it is fitting that it be already shut up in each man's storehouses. The season of good harvests has passed, the beginning of winter is already rising, plants wither and flowers fade. Come, then, let us transfer what belongs to the season to ourselves and say this: as this age is already creeping toward its end, and the time hangs over us, as it were, and is about to break in, the time when the lovers of sin must be punished, each one, if he is wise, will heap up the fruit of his own labors and bring it into the treasuries above. He will remember Christ saying: ‘Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy and where thieves break in and steal; but rather store up treasures in heaven’ (Matthew 6:19–20). So, since, now that Christ has been raised, the words of the holy teachers of the mysteries bring us to remember the consummation (for they have cried aloud up and down, ‘It is the last hour’ (1 John 2:18)), let what belongs to each, it says, be gathered from now on into the treasuries above. But ‘on the new moon,’ it says, ‘of the month in which you shut up the crops, you shall have a rest, a memorial of trumpets.’ For each one stores up the good things won by his own sweat, and will take thought and care for the delight and rest that last forever, remembering that, as the inspired Paul says…
